subject: Dedicated capacity: soft-cap, burst billing, and sample terms
messages:
From: Tom Archer <tom.archer@nimbushealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Question: what happens if we spike above our committed pool?

Hi Aditya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two quick follow-ups from procurement before we move to legal/SOW:

1) If we exceed our committed GPU pool (say a 30% spike for a day), what enforcement do you apply? Do you throttle, queue, or automatically bill overage?
2) How do you meter bursts vs. steady-state overage? We need predictable invoicing for budgeting.
3) Any flexibility on the overage rate if we sign a 12–24 month commit? We may be able to push a larger commit in exchange for softer overage terms.

Appreciate a concise example (numbers) and any sample language we can show our procurement/legal team.

—Tom
Tom Archer
Dir., Cloud Operations
NimbusHealth
Attachments: nimbus_request_summary.txt (1 KB: short notes)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Tom Archer <tom.archer@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: what happens if we spike above our committed pool?

Tom —

Thanks — good questions. High level summary first, then a compact numeric example and proposed contractual language you can share with procurement/legal.

High level:
- Commit model: you reserve a GPU pool (e.g., 8 x A100-equivalent slots) with guaranteed throughput and latency SLOs. Billing for the commit is monthly at the agreed reserved price.
- Burst handling: we provide a configurable soft-cap (burst buffer) and temporary autoscale/burst capacity for short spikes. Bursts are metered separately from committed consumption.
- Enforcement: short, unexpected spikes use the burst buffer. If the buffer is exhausted we apply a two-stage behavior: soft throttling (priority-preserving) + overage billing. Long sustained overages trigger rate-limited throttling to protect underlying tenants unless you opt-in for burst-reserve billing.

Numeric example (for illustration only):
- Commit: 8-slot pool (baseline) at $28,000/month (example price).
- Monthly "grace bucket": 100 GPU-hours included for free to cover transient spikes (configurable).
- Bursts beyond grace bucket but within 25% above commit in a 24-hour window: billed at a reduced overage multiplier (first-tier) = 1.25x of list per-GPU-hour rate.
- Sustained usage above 25% for more than 72 hours in a 30-day window: billed at full overage = 1.5x list per-GPU-hour and subject to soft throttling if not approved for permanent capacity increase.
- Invoice cadence: true-up monthly with real-time reporting in the Console + alerts at 75/90/100% of commit.

What we can put in an SOW (short sample clause):
"Redwood will provide a monthly committed GPU pool as set forth in Appendix A. For transient usage spikes, Customer will have access to a monthly Grace Bucket of GPU-hours. Usage above the Grace Bucket but within a 25% burst allowance in any 24-hour period will be billed at 1.25x the standard per-GPU-hour rate. Usage that exceeds the 25% allowance for a period longer than seventy-two (72) consecutive hours in a thirty (30) day period will be billed at 1.5x the standard per-GPU-hour rate and may be subject to soft throttling to preserve platform stability unless Customer and Redwood agree to increase committed capacity."

Attachments: I've attached a provisional pricing sheet and a short draft of the soft-cap terms to review internally.

Open to negotiation — if Nimbus can commit to a 12–24 month reserved level we can discuss reducing the 1.25x multiplier to 1.15x for the first 12 months and enlarge the Grace Bucket.

Next steps: If this looks reasonable I can loop in our legal/finance of record and put a redlineable SOW together.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_softcap_terms.pdf (2 pages), provisional_pricing_sheet.xlsx (6 rows)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Re: Question: what happens if we spike above our committed pool?

Aditya —

Quick internal note on negotiation posture:
- Offer: 12-month commit + expanded grace bucket (200 GPU-hours) in exchange for introductory overage multipliers: 1.15x for first 10% overage, 1.3x thereafter (cap at 1.3x for year one).
- Include 30-day rolling true-up and a single invoice credit for any overage that persists >60 days and is attributable to onboarding automation bugs (we can gate this).
- Finance wants a clean place in SOW that says "alerts and real-time usage reporting"; procurement will push back if there's any opaque usage math.

If Tom pushes for lower multipliers, we can concede to 1.10x on the first tier for strictly limited initial months but require a minimum 12-month commit and a write-in for long-term capacity review.

—Laura
From: Tom Archer <tom.archer@nimbushealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: NimbusHealth Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Question: what happens if we spike above our committed pool?

Aditya / Laura —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A few follow-ups from procurement after reviewing:
1) Grace bucket: can you make that 200 GPU-hours/month bundled for the first 12 months if we sign a 12-month commit at the proposed price?
2) Overage multipliers: 1.25x/1.5x is a little high for budgeting. We'd prefer a stepped approach where the first 10% above commit is 1.10x, the next 15% is 1.25x, and anything beyond that is 1.4x.
3) Billing predictability: we require a 30-day notice and a "sustained overage cap" mechanism where if projected overage will exceed $X in the coming 30 days we get an automated hold and an approval flow before charges are applied.

Also, can you confirm how network egress and any storage-attached costs are handled in the SOW — procurement flagged those as separate line items.

If we can get to a firm proposal on those three points, procurement is comfortable moving to legal.

—Tom
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Tom Archer <tom.archer@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: what happens if we spike above our committed pool? — proposed reconciliation

Tom —

Thanks — good, actionable feedback. Summary of what Redwood can commit to as a starting position to move into legal (we'll put this in a redline-ready SOW appendix):

Agreed commercial outline (proposed):
- Term: 12 months committed pool.
- Grace bucket: 200 GPU-hours/month included for months 1–12.
- Overage tiers (month true-up):
  * 0–10% above monthly commit: 1.10x per-GPU-hour
  * >10%–25% above monthly commit: 1.25x per-GPU-hour
  * >25% above monthly commit: 1.40x per-GPU-hour and subject to an agreed throttle-review; Redwood will not throttle without providing a 48-hour notice and proposed remediation options.
- Sustained overage governance: if projected overage will exceed the Monthly Commit + Grace Bucket by more than $20k in the next 30 days, Redwood will open an automatic hold and notify Nimbus with a recommended mitigation (temporary scale increase or scheduling changes). Charges will not be applied until Nimbus approves the hold removal or 72 hours elapse after notification.
- Network egress and attached storage: remain separate line items — we will itemize them on the monthly invoice with consumption details.
- Monitoring & alerts: real-time visibility in Redwood Console, alerting at 75/90/100% with webhook/hands-on escalation options.
- Introductory concession: Redwood will honor the above tiered overage pricing for months 1–12 of the agreement. After month 12, parties will enter a capacity review and reprice as appropriate.

Next steps: I'll draft a compact Appendix A (pricing & burst terms) and circulate a DocuSign link for the SOW once legal/finance review is complete. Laura/Neha — can you confirm internal sign-off on the $20k threshold and the 48/72-hour notification windows so I can lock this?

Tom — if that reads OK I'll send the SOW draft to procurement/legal by EOD Monday and include the HubSpot deal link (see attached).

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
